bodyHtml:
Our 2022 Annual Report covers the foundation’s first year, from its start in July 2022. It includes our executive summary, facts and financials, certifications, partners and board of directors. The full text of the report is below, and you can download the original report at the end of this page.

Executive summary

Welcome to the Victoria Venezuela Foundation! We are a non-profit organization 501(c)(3), dedicated to embed the love of Jesus to our most vulnerable children in Venezuela, bringing to each community critical food and medical attention.

Since our inception in July 2022, we firmly placed our hearts to God and commenced planting our initial seeds with a clear mission - design a local support network investing in the well being of these children and the future of Venezuela.

We have been humbled and appreciative of the overwhelming support by the community, volunteers and companies propelling the faith and establishing strong core and long-term values for these children.

Our passionate and relentless team established two local support centers in: Los Valles del Tuy, Miranda and Ciudad Bolivar, Bolivar supporting both food and medical attention programs. Below is a brief snapshot of the work that was accomplished in 2022:

  • +5,000 nutritional plates served to at risk children
  • 52 children received critical medical attention
  • 5 companies investing and sponsoring support programs

We can’t wait to see the new thousand smiles and filled hearts this new year with your continued support. We look forward to 2023 with an even stronger determination and abundant faith on what God continues to do in Venezuela.

Randy & Helen
Founders

Facts and financials

We are proud to launch this year incorporating an efficient financial structure. The foundation implemented a zero ($0) Administration cost framework; enabling the use of your contributions and maximize impact to both food and medical attention Charitable Programs [~89 cents of every dollar donated directly support these children]

The logos of the donation platforms appear in the full report.

Certifications

Victoria Venezuela Foundation was formally certified as an exemplary organization (Silver Rating) by GuideStar.

The candid seal is the highest possible rating and indicates a nonprofit’s exceeding industry standards, this exceptional designation sets us apart and demonstrates our trustworthiness to the public

Partners

Centro Cristiano Luz de Las Naciones (CCLN) is a Ministry founded over 30 years ago in Los Valles Del Tuy, Miranda Venezuela. MVV together with Pastor Jose Guerrero, launched 12 different nutrition centers across the city supporting over 400 children every week.

Una Comida por una Sonrisa, is a non-profit foundation that has been providing support to local children in Ciudad Bolivar, Bolivar Venezuela. Led by Edneivys Medina, and with support from the Victoria Venezuela Foundation, we have established a medical attention Support Program supporting 52 babies and young children in the area.

Company sponsors

In 2022, the foundation received a strong endorsement by companies supporting both food and health care programs across the local support network nationwide

The logos of our company sponsors appear in the full report.

Frequently asked questions

What did Victoria Venezuela Foundation achieve in 2022?

More than 5,000 nutritional plates were served to at-risk children, 52 children received critical medical attention, and 5 companies invested in and sponsored the support programs.

How much went to charitable programs in 2022?

$5,869, or 89% of donations. Fundraising, advertising and other expenses were $696, or 11%.

Does the foundation spend money on administration?

The report shows $0 in administration costs in 2022, under the foundation’s zero administration cost framework.

It includes our impact highlights, corporate sponsors, donation platforms, financials, certifications, partners and team. The full text of the report is below, and you can download the original report at the end of this page.

A message from us

As we reflect on our journey in 2023, it has been incredible to witness first hand how our community continues to come together in support of children and Venezuela. We commenced our year with an unwavering commitment to our mission: Design support networks throughout Venezuela with nutrition and medical attention programs while teaching children to have a personal relationship with Jesus Christ.

Our volunteers and partners continued to grow with a vivid calling to serve and make a difference. We wanted to extend our heartfelt appreciation for your partnership and generous support. We delivered and exceeded expectations across the support programs bringing joy and hope to children’s lives.

Below is a brief snapshot of the work that together we accomplished in 2023:

  • +24,800 nutritional plates served to at risk children
  • +500 Babies and children received critical medical attention
  • 15 corporations sponsoring support programs and investing in Venezuela

At each of the support centers across, we could see each week how children’s lives were being transformed. Their palpable desire to attend at first in desperate need of help. Little by little, we could see a light being ignited as they commence their journey to learn more about their heavenly Father, God.

As the team commences this new year, with great anticipation, we look forward to continue being part of the transformative work that God is doing in Venezuela. We hope you are as well. We have big plans and dreams for these children’s future, and we invite you to join us in this journey of faith and love.

With blessings,
Randy & Helen

card.title: How to sponsor a child directly, without going through a large charity
card.excerpt: Direct child sponsorship means your monthly gift supports an identified child through a specific organization, and you can see where the money goes.

image.alt: How to sponsor a child directly, without going through a large charity

title: How to sponsor a child directly, without going through a large charity

authors.name: Randy Lander
authors.role: Founder and Chairman, Victoria Venezuela Foundation

image.alt: Five boys at a Victoria Venezuela Foundation meal table in Venezuela, giving a thumbs up over bowls of pasta.

bodyHtml:
The short answer

Direct child sponsorship means your monthly gift supports an identified child through a specific organization, and you can see where the money goes. Large US programs ask $39 to $43 a month. The main trade-off against a large international charity is scale versus proximity: big organizations have more infrastructure, smaller ones can tell you the name of the person who handed a child their meal.

At Victoria Venezuela Foundation, sponsorship starts at $25 a month. Your sponsorship connects you with one child, and gifts fund the nutrition, medical care and education programs that reach every child in our care. In fiscal 2025, 95% of funds went directly to programs.

What “sponsoring a child” actually means

Child sponsorship is a recurring monthly donation connected to a specific child. In most programs the sponsor receives updates, and often letters or photographs, so the relationship is visible rather than abstract.

What it does not mean, and this is the most common misunderstanding: your money does not go to that child as cash. It funds the programs that child is enrolled in. A $25 monthly gift does not become $25 in a family’s hands. It becomes a share of a meal program, a clinic visit, a set of school supplies.

That distinction matters because it is also what makes sponsorship work. Programs serve groups. A child benefits because the program around them exists, and pooled gifts keep support steady for every child even when a sponsor steps away.

Why people look for a direct option

Three reasons come up repeatedly.

  • They want to know where the money goes. Large charities publish audited financials, which is genuinely more than most small ones do. But the answer arrives as a percentage in an annual report, not as a photograph of the classroom.
  • They want a real connection. Sponsors who have given for years often say they never heard from the child in a way that felt personal.
  • They want their money concentrated. A smaller organization working in one country puts more of each dollar into a place the donor chose deliberately.

None of those are arguments that large charities are bad. They are large because they are effective at scale, and scale saves lives. They are arguments about what a particular donor is looking for.

Direct sponsorship compared with a large international charity

Small, direct organizationLarge international charity
Typical monthly costVaries (ours starts at $25)$39 to $43
Countries servedUsually oneOften 20 or more
Communication with the childOften direct and informalStructured, usually mediated
Financial reportingVaries; ask for itAudited and published annually
Third-party rating availableSometimesAlmost always
Ability to visitSometimes possibleRare, and usually a formal trip

Large-charity costs are the published monthly rates of World Vision, Plan International USA, Children International and Compassion International, as of September 2026. Check each organization’s current rate.

How to sponsor a child directly, step by step

  1. Pick a country or a cause, not an organization. Start with where you want the money to go. The list of organizations narrows quickly once you do.
  2. Verify the organization is a registered charity. In the United States that means a 501(c)(3) designation and an EIN. You can check any EIN for free on the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search, ProPublica’s Nonprofit Explorer, or Candid.
  3. Read the most recent Form 990. It is a public document. You are looking for what share of spending goes to programs rather than fundraising and administration.
  4. Ask what your money funds, specifically. A good organization can answer in one sentence. A vague answer is itself an answer.
  5. Ask what you will receive and how often. Letters, photographs, progress reports. Get the cadence in writing.
  6. Ask what happens if you stop. A well-run program has a plan for it. See the FAQ below.
  7. Set up the gift and keep the receipt. In the US, contributions to a 501(c)(3) are tax-deductible.

The question that tells you the most is the simplest one: what does my $25 buy this month? An organization that can answer it precisely is one that knows what it is doing.

How to check a charity before you give

You do not have to take anyone’s word for it. Four free sources:

  • IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search. Confirms 501(c)(3) status and that the organization is in good standing.
  • ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer. Publishes Form 990 filings, so you can see revenue and spending.
  • Candid, formerly GuideStar. Transparency ratings based on what the organization voluntarily discloses.
  • Charity Navigator. Ratings and financial analysis, though smaller organizations are sometimes unrated simply because of their size.

An organization that has not been rated is not necessarily a bad one. Ratings often require a revenue threshold. But an organization that will not show you its 990 is a different matter.

About Victoria Venezuela FoundationWe are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit based in Weston, Florida. Our EIN is 88-3282100. We hold a Candid Platinum Transparency seal, and in fiscal 2025, 95% of funds went directly to programs. Our annual reports are published on this site under Resources › Financials.

Frequently asked questions

How much does it cost to sponsor a child?

Large US programs ask $39 to $43 a month. At Victoria Venezuela Foundation, sponsorship starts at $25 a month.

What does my sponsorship actually pay for?

Your gifts fund three programs: a weekly nutrition program, medical attention twice a year, and an annual education program. Since 2022 they have served 77,300 meals, provided 1,012 medical visits for children and supported 99 children in school. The money funds the programs the child is enrolled in rather than going to the family as cash.

Is child sponsorship tax-deductible?

In the United States, yes, if the organization is a registered 501(c)(3). Victoria Venezuela Foundation is, under EIN 88-3282100. Keep your receipts.

What happens if I have to stop sponsoring?

Nothing happens to the child immediately. Well-run programs do not withdraw services when a sponsor leaves; gifts are pooled precisely so support stays steady while a new sponsor is found. Tell the organization rather than cancelling silently, so they can plan.

Can I write to the child I sponsor?

Yes. You can exchange letters with the child you sponsor and learn more about their life. You also see them grow through photos of our activities, and you can join our regular prayers for them.

Can I choose which child I sponsor?

Yes. Browse the children waiting for a sponsor and choose.

How is a small charity different from a large one?

Scale versus proximity. Large organizations have more infrastructure, more countries and audited reporting. Small ones can usually tell you more about the specific child and the specific place. Neither is automatically better.

bodyHtml:
Our 2025 Impact Report covers a year of work with more than 700 children in Venezuela. It includes our programs, our partners, our team and our condensed financials. The full text of the report is below, and you can download the original report at the end of this page.

A message from us

This 2025 was a beautiful testament witnessing love in action. Every smile, every moment of renewed hope, and every story of transformation reminded us why this mission matters so deeply. Our hearts are overflowing with gratitude for all that God allowed us to sow and pour into the lives of our 700+ children throughout 2025.

Week after week, our extraordinary volunteers showed up with unwavering dedication and excellence in all they do — preparing centers, serving meals, teaching, encouraging, and creating safe spaces filled with love. Their servant hearts fueled with love are the foundation of everything we do, and we are profoundly grateful for the countless hours they invested to ensure every child felt valued and supported. As scripture teaches us:

“You are the light of the world. Let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.”
Matthew 5:14–16

This year also marked several major milestones that strengthened our support programs and impact:

  • Launched new nutrition support initiatives, extending kitchen infrastructure, tables and chairs helping increase the number of children receiving consistent meals
  • Expanded educational development programs, recognizing and celebrating the top 10% students and their academic performance
  • Golf Charity Tournament hosted 1st edition in Weston Hills, Florida joining over 40 corporate partners, providing the financial stability for long-term growth.
  • Enhanced technology integration and reporting systems, ensuring transparency, accountability, and readiness for scaling.

To our volunteers, strategic partners, and supporters: thank you for walking with us in faith and believing in this mission. Thank you for investing in these children and in Venezuela. Together, we are building futures filled with hope — making ways, one child and one family at a time.

With blessings,
Randy & Helen
Founders

Who we are

We are a non-profit foundation, 501(c)(3) Tax ID: 88-3282100, dedicated to paving the way for the most vulnerable children in Venezuela through its nutrition, medical care and education programs. Currently, two Support Centers have been established in Venezuela: Los Valles del Tuy, Miranda and Ciudad Bolívar, Bolívar.

We operate with a holistic and integrated approach with the Christian faith as the cornerstone of everything we do. We partner with local churches to provide guiding principles and values to the children we serve. Our cohesive support programs are designed to address the critical needs of children, helping to transform their future and enabling them to become a light to the world (Matthew 5:14).

Our Vision

Pave the way for vulnerable children throughout Venezuela by training them with biblical principles so that they can be light in the world.

Mission

Design support networks throughout Venezuela through food, medical care and education programs while teaching children to have a personal relationship with Jesus Christ

Our commitment

At the Victoria Venezuela Foundation, we are committed to making a significant impact in the lives of those most in need. We wholeheartedly believe that all children were made in the image of God. Children should be valued, respected and loved as God has shown us with his only son Jesus Christ.

The UN adopted the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, an opportunity for countries and their societies to embark on a new path to improve the lives of all people, leaving no one behind. Our team works on three (3) critical goals: zero hunger, good health and well-being and quality education to support the development of each child.

Governance policies and standards

Victoria Venezuela Foundation is dedicated to transparency across all its operations. By establishing clear policies and governance through the Board of Directors and the entire organization, we aim to successfully address effectiveness and risks.

Key policies and standards include:

  • Conflict of Interest Policy
  • Administration Cost Policy
  • Risk Management
  • Non-Discrimination Policy
  • Data Protection and Document Retention Policy

VVF is certified by the leading non-profit regulatory institutions.

Major annual achievements included the (Platinum Rating) by GuideStar as an exemplary organization.

The Seal of Candidacy is the highest rating possible and indicates that a nonprofit exceeds industry standards. Only the top 15% of organizations receive Platinum status. We are honored to be the leading nonprofit in Venezuela with this recognition.

bodyHtml:
Your Impact 1Q2024 is our update on the first quarter of 2024, with results for the year to date. The full text of the report is below, and you can download the original report at the end of this page.

Your Impact - 1Q2024

Weston, Florida (April 18, 2024) – Victoria Venezuela Foundation is pleased to announce the continued progress during first quarter of 2024. We are thrilled to share our accomplishments and express our heartfelt gratitude to all our supporters and sponsors who have made this possible.

Year to date, Victoria Venezuela Foundation achieved the following milestones:

  • Nutrition Program: We are proud to have provided 4,780 nutritious meals to vulnerable children, ensuring they receive the nourishment they need to thrive.
  • Medical Attention Program: Our dedicated team of volunteers and medical professionals attended to 150 children, offering them essential medical care, improving their health, and providing them with hope for a brighter future.
  • Church Attendance: 81 new children participating in weekly services.
  • Mission trip: Concluded a pivotal visit to Venezuela. The collaboration bore fruit with the initiation of several innovative programs:
    • An annual program featuring 12 workshops for the Foundation’s Ministry leaders in Venezuela.
    • Provision of books and digital resources by One Hope “Avivamiento” to bolster the Foundation’s educational programs.
    • The launch of the "Feed" program, aimed at nurturing young team leaders to support the Foundation's growth plans.
  • Media: Our founder, Randy Lander appeared on the national radio program 88.9 FM. He shared insights into the Foundation's progress and its ambitious growth plan for 2024.

Victoria Venezuela Foundation remains dedicated to our mission: Design support networks throughout Venezuela with food and medical care programs while teaching children to have a personal relationship with Jesus Christ. We look forward to continuing our efforts with the same passion and commitment for the future of the Children in Venezuela.

For more information or to get involved with our cause, please visit our website at https://victoriavenezuelafoundation.org or contact us at media@victoriavenezuelafoundation.org

Frequently asked questions

How many meals did the foundation serve in the first quarter of 2024?

4,780 nutritious meals to vulnerable children, year to date.

How many children received medical attention?

The foundation’s volunteers and medical professionals attended to 150 children, year to date.

What came out of the mission trip to Venezuela?

An annual program of 12 workshops for the foundation’s ministry leaders in Venezuela, books and digital resources from One Hope “Avivamiento” for the educational programs, and the launch of the "Feed" program for young team leaders.

Your Impact 1Q2025 is our update on the first quarter of 2025, with results for the year to date. The full text of the report is below, and you can download the original report at the end of this page.

Your Impact – 1Q2025

Weston, Florida (April 23, 2025) –Victoria Venezuela Foundation is pleased to announce the continued progress during the first quarter of 2025. We are thrilled to share our accomplishments and express our heartfelt gratitude to all our supporters and sponsors who have made this possible.

Year to date, Victoria Venezuela Foundation achieved the following milestones:

  • Nutrition Program: We are proud to have provided over 6,367 nutritious meals to vulnerable children, ensuring they receive the nourishment they need to thrive.
  • Medical Attention Program: Our dedicated team of volunteers and medical professionals attended to over 110 children, offering them essential medical care, improving their health, and providing them with hope and love for a brighter future.
  • Church Attendance: 385 children participating in weekly services.
  • New Corporate Sponsors: We proudly welcome Top Golf and Triumphant Transition Partners as our new corporate partners.
  • Candid GuideStar: For a 3rd consecutive year, received “Platinum Rating” while also being the leading organization in Venezuela with this recognition.
  • New Teammates: Welcomed our new Chief Technology officer, Enrique Flores and Directors of Business Development, Julio Garcia and Archange Merveille, surpassing now over 100+ volunteers being part of the organization.
  • Strategic Collaboration: Joined and secure a strategic membership and alliance with the Venezuelan-American Chamber of Commerce of the United States

For more information or to get involved with our cause, please visit our website at https://victoriavenezuelafoundation.org or contact us at media@victoriavenezuelafoundation.org

About the Victoria Venezuela Foundation

The Victoria Venezuela Foundation is a nonprofit organization committed to supporting Venezuela’s most vulnerable children through programs in nutrition, healthcare, and education, based on Christian principles. Currently, the Foundation has two support centers in Venezuela. With the help of its sponsors and partners, the Foundation continues working to provide these children with a future full of hope and opportunities.

Your Impact - 3Q2024

Weston, Florida (Oct 18, 2024) – Victoria Venezuela Foundation is pleased to announce the continued progress during third quarter of 2024. We are thrilled to share our accomplishments and express our heartfelt gratitude to all our supporters who have made this possible.

Year to date, Victoria Venezuela Foundation achieved the following milestones:

  • Nutrition Program: We are proud to have provided 16,797 nutritious meals to vulnerable children, ensuring they receive the nourishment they need to thrive.
  • Medical Attention Program: Our dedicated team of volunteers and medical professionals attended to 350 children, offering them essential medical care, improving their health, and providing them with hope for a brighter future
  • Education Program: excited to announce the launch of an impactful education program empowering vulnerable children in the Los Valles del Tuy, Miranda community. This initiative aims to provide essential school supplies, including backpacks, thermoses, pencils, and more, enabling these 24 children to reach their God-given potential.
  • FestiKids: A Heartwarming Celebration drawing over 378 children in Ciudad Bolivar, Bolivar. This vibrant event dedicated to bringing love and compassion. The celebration was a resounding success, a day filled with joy, community spirit, and care. FestiKids offered a variety of activities designed to uplift and entertain, including fun games, arts and crafts, and engaging storytelling that shared the Word of God. The event not only provided children with essential food and clothing but also included complimentary haircuts, ensuring every child left feeling valued and refreshed.

We extend our heartfelt thanks to our donors, volunteers, and sponsors for their unwavering support. Your contributions have made a significant difference in the lives of vulnerable children, and we could not have achieved these milestones without you.

Victoria Venezuela Foundation remains dedicated to our mission: Design support networks throughout Venezuela with food and medical care programs while teaching children to have a personal relationship with Jesus Christ. We look forward to continuing our efforts with the same passion and commitment for the future of the Children in Venezuela.
